In [[set theory]], a '''normal measure''' is a measure on a [[measurable cardinal]] <math>\kappa</math> such that the equivalence class of the identity function on <math>\kappa</math> maps to <math>\kappa</math> itself in the [[ultraproduct|ultrapower]] construction. Equivalently, a measure <math>\mu</math> on <math>\kappa</math> is normal iff whenever <math>f:\kappa\to\kappa</math> is such that <math>f(\alpha)<\alpha</math> for <math>\mu</math>-many <math>\alpha<\kappa</math>, then there is a <math>\beta<\kappa</math> such that <math>f(\alpha)=\beta</math> for <math>\mu</math>-many <math>\alpha<\kappa</math>. (Here, "<math>\mu</math>-many" means that the set of elements of <math>\kappa</math> where the property holds is a member of the ultrafilter, i.e. has measure 1 in <math>\mu</math>.) Also equivalent, the ultrafilter (set of sets with measure 1) is closed under [[diagonal intersection]].

For a normal measure <math>\mu</math>, any [[club set|closed unbounded]] (club) subset of <math>\kappa</math> contains <math>\mu</math>-many ordinals less than <math>\kappa</math> and any subset containing <math>\mu</math>-many ordinals less than <math>\kappa</math> is stationary in <math>\kappa</math>.

If an uncountable cardinal <math>\kappa</math> has a measure on it, then it has a normal measure on it.
